worldspawn music key of maps/kaos2.bsp, naming a track no pinned OpenArena release ships. The key carries no file extension, so S_CodecGetSound probes the stem against wav, ogg and opus and then reports the name exactly as it was passed, without one (ioq3 code/client/snd_codec.c). CG_StartMusic hands CS_MUSIC to trap_S_StartBackgroundTrack, which never reaches S_RegisterSound, so the two S_RegisterSound spellings cannot occur for it; what the backends differ in is the rest. The OpenAL client prints the codec line alone, while the dma backend adds "couldn't open music file music/fla22k_05" from S_OpenBackgroundStream (ioq3 code/client/snd_dma.c) - a line no acceptance classifies, recorded as such in scripts/arena_acceptance.py. A missing track is silence, not a failure

the same track under a second name, written as a 'music' key on two func_door entities of maps/kaos2.bsp - two more keys in the entity lump, not a second lookup of the worldspawn value, because nothing appends an extension to the name the engine *reports*: S_CodecGetSound prints the filename as it was passed (ioq3 code/client/snd_codec.c). The closure reads 'music' and 'noise' off every entity (scripts/content_pack.py _add_bsp), which is the conservative reading; the engine reads a 'music' key from no entity but the world. 'music' is not in the game's spawn-field table, so G_ParseField drops it, and SP_worldspawn is the only code that asks for one (ioq3 code/game/g_spawn.c), so this name is never indexed, never opened and never reported missing. It does appear in a developer-level log, where S_CodecUtilOpen prints "Can't read sound file music/fla22k_05.wav" as one of the three codec attempts made for the *worldspawn* stem - the same spelling arriving from the other reference, not this key being read. Declared here because the closure sees it, and recorded as unreachable in tests/test_arena_runtime.py rather than given an engine note for a line that cannot occur

a texture named by the shader lump of maps/kaos2.bsp that no pinned archive provides and no shipped shader script defines. Nothing renders through it: R_LoadShaders only byte-swaps the flags, so a shader-lump entry reaches shader registration through ShaderForShaderNum alone - which calls R_FindShaderEx, the function R_FindShader wraps - once per surface (ioq3 code/renderergl2/tr_bsp.c), and none of this BSP's 2,194 surfaces indexes entry 48. The three other ways a name can be registered without the shader lump name it either: a fog record carries its own shader string, and this BSP's single record names textures/liquids/lavahell_750; R_LoadEntities passes worldspawn 'remapshader' and 'vertexremapshader' values to R_RemapShader; and 'targetShaderName'/'targetShaderNewName' are spawn fields, so G_UseTargets can remap a shader at run time over CS_SHADERSTATE (ioq3 code/game/g_utils.c, code/cgame/cg_servercmds.c). This BSP writes none of those four keys. So the name is never registered, the audit's face share is 0 of 2,194, and the engine reports nothing - not even at PRINT_DEVELOPER
